title: Fritto Misto di Mare
subtitle: Mixed fried seafood with light batter and lemon
excerpt: Fritto misto di mare is a mixed platter of battered and deep-fried seafood: squid rings, prawns, and whitebait fried in a light, crisp batter and served immediately with lemon wedges and flaked salt. It is the defining fried seafood dish of the Italian coast and requires a thermometer and fresh oil for the batter to stay crisp.
sourceNotes: Fritto misto di mare is a staple of Italian coastal cooking throughout the Adriatic and Ligurian coasts. Pellegrino Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, includes multiple fried seafood preparations.

content.text: Fritto misto di mare depends on three things: very fresh seafood, oil at exactly 180C, and eating it immediately. The batter is minimal so the seafood flavour comes through. The seafood goes in small batches; crowding the pan drops the oil temperature and produces soggy batter rather than crisp.

items.prepNote: cleaned, bodies cut into rings, tentacles left whole

content.text: Heat the oil and make the batter
Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of vegetable oil in a large, deep saucepan to 180C. Use a thermometer to monitor the temperature throughout.

Whisk {{plain-flour}} of plain flour, {{sparkling-water}} of ice-cold sparkling water, and {{salt-table}} of salt together until a smooth, thin batter forms. Do not overmix. The batter should coat the back of a spoon lightly. Keep the batter cold.

Pat all the seafood dry. Working in small batches, dip {{whitebait}} whitebait into the batter and lower into the oil. Fry for 2 minutes until golden. Drain on kitchen paper. Repeat with {{squid}} squid rings and {{prawns-raw}} prawns, frying each for 2 to 3 minutes until crisp.
Season immediately with {{salt-flakes}} of flaked salt and serve at once with {{lemon}} lemon wedges. Fritto misto waits for no one.

items.symptom: The batter is soggy rather than crisp
items.cause: The oil was not hot enough, or too much seafood was added at once, which dropped the oil temperature.
items.fix: Fry in small batches and allow the oil to return to 180C between batches. The batter only crisps above 170C.

items.symptom: The batter is thick and heavy
items.cause: The batter was too thick or was allowed to warm up.
items.fix: The batter should be thin enough to see the seafood through it. Add more cold sparkling water to thin it and keep the bowl over ice if the kitchen is warm.

content.text: Fritto misto di mare is the central dish of Italian coastal street food and restaurant cooking. Every port town on the Adriatic, Ligurian, and Sicilian coasts has its own version, varying the seafood mix according to what was landed that day. In Venice it is sold in paper cones from street stalls (frìto misto alla veneziana). The light sparkling-water batter is a modern refinement of the older flour-and-water approach; both work, but the sparkling version stays crisper longer as the carbon dioxide creates small pockets of lightness.
